_about: Alerting policy: WHEN the system raises, clears and groups alerts. Changing this file changes behavior without touching code. Every key is explained in docs/ALERTING.md. Times are in milliseconds (keys end in Ms). Restart the backend after editing; it checks this file at startup and refuses to start if a value is invalid.

thresholds._about: WHAT counts as bad. These are the starting values for the dashboard's Settings tab, which can change them while running. A sensor's own thresholds in layout.json win over these.

defaults._about: Applies to every alert unless its rule below says otherwise. oneOffEventCooldownMs: minimum time between repeats of a one-off event (sudden Wi-Fi drop, temperature spike) on the same device.

rules._about: Per alert. alertAfterMs: how long a problem must last before it is an alert (0 = first bad reading). clearAfterMs: how long it must stay fixed before the alert clears. clearMargin: how far past the threshold a value must recover before it counts as fixed, in the metric's own unit.

grouping._about: One cause, one incident. Alerts are held for waitMs so related ones can arrive; signal problems on the same radio band then become one incident.

silence._about: What happens when a device goes quiet. The sensor watchdog itself is thresholds.watchdogTimeout.

rf._about: Radio health. A device's normal rhythm is learned from its own heartbeat. A gap is a silence longer than gapAfterIntervals × that rhythm (and at least thresholds.gapThresholdMs); a burst is readings arriving closer together than burstUnderInterval × the rhythm.

drones._about: A drone's silence is judged against its mission: landed at home after the route is normal, anything else is an alert.

audience._about: Phones in the audience demo. AUDIENCE_WATCHDOG_MS and AUDIENCE_AUTO_PURGE_MS environment variables still override these.
